glosses: gerund of umpolen
to reverse the polarity of
эл.-техн. переключать полюса; менять полярность
перен. изменить (что-л.); передумать
Inverser la polarité électrique ou magnétique.
senses.note: Le terme n’a pas de connotation d’erreur ou de manipulation fautive ; le terme dans ce cas est verpolen

examples.text: Polt man eine Diode um, ändert sich ihr Verhalten von leitend zu sperrend und umgekehrt. Dagegen ändert sich die Kennlinie eines Widerstandes nicht, wenn man ihn umpolt.
examples.translation: Si l’on inverse la polarité d’une diode son comportement se modifie de passant à bloquant et vice-versa. En revanche, la réponse d’une résistance ne change pas si l’on inverse sa polarité.

examples.text: Viele Gleichstrommotoren ändern ihre Drehrichtung, wenn man sie umpolt.
examples.translation: Beaucoup de moteurs à courant continu changent leur direction de rotation quand on inverse leur polarité.

glosses: Inverser la polarité d’un groupe fonctionnel en chimie organique (voir umpolung / Umpolung).

examples.text: In der Organozinn-Chemie ist bekannt, dass sich die Trialkylzinnhalogenide bei der Reaktion mit Alkalimetallen gut umpolen lassen, und so die entsprechenden Stannide liefern.
examples.translation: Dans la chimie des organoétains, il est connu que la polarité des halogénures de trialkylétain peut être facilement inversée par réaction avec des métaux alcalins, ce qui donne les stannures correpondants.

glosses: Changer complètement, radicalement, inverser la manière de voir ou de penser, inverser l’opinion ou le comportement.

examples.text: Bei sogenannten Konversionstherapien sollten Lesben und Schwule zu Heteros "umgepolt" werden.
examples.translation: Dans les dénommées thérapies de conversion, les lesbiennes et gays devraient "inversés" en hétéros.

glosses: Changement radical d’une organisation, par exemple de la politique d’un pays.

examples.text: Margaret Thatcher wollte die Wirtschaft des Vereinigten Königreichs völlig zum Neoliberalismus umpolen.
examples.translation: Margaret Thatcher voulait changer radicalement l’économie du Royaume-Uni vers le néolibéralisme.

examples.text: Die Kinder des Firmengründers haben das Traditionsunternehmen zu einem der innovativsten Hersteller umgepolt.
examples.translation: Les enfants du fondateur ont transformé radicalement l’entreprise traditionnelle en un des fabricants les plus innovants.

glosses: elektrische oder magnetische Pole vertauschen

examples.text: Als er bei einem Sonnenuntergang "Faust" rezitierte - "sie rückt und weicht / und fördert neues Leben" -, fuhr ihm wie ein Blitz durch das Gehirn, dass man mit mehrphasigem Wechselstrom ein rotierendes Magnetfeld erzeugen und mit ihm einen Elektromotor treiben kann (man kann es auch mit Gleichstrom, man muss ihn aber immer wieder umpolen).
Sie beschleunigen die durchfliegenden Elektronen und Positronen, indem sie im Bruchteil von Sekunden elektrische Felder in den Kammern umpolen, die die Teilchen entweder anziehen oder abstoßen.
Ihre Anzahl schwankt in einem Elfjahreszyklus, gekoppelt an das Magnetfeld der Sonne, das sich alle elf Jahre umpolt.

glosses: jemanden vom gegenteiligen Standpunkt überzeugen, zum Gegenteil verändern

examples.text: Neben Anzeigen- und Plakatwerbung sowie einer Online-Plattform umfasst die Kampagne auch TV-Spots, deren Protagonisten gut 30 deutsche Prominente sind, die honorarfrei werben: Unter anderem wollen National-Torhüter Oliver Kahn, Literaturkritiker Marcel Reich-Ranicki, Talk-Ikone Harald Schmidt und Ex-Eisprinzessin Katarina Witt deutsche Miesepeter umpolen.
Der Privatsender will in seiner neuen Show "Österreich isst gesund" ganze Betriebe und Dörfer ernährungstechnisch umpolen.
Lesben sollten umgepolt und Schwule in Heteros verwandelt werden.

glosses: Dinge ins Gegenteil verkehren, grundlegend verändern

examples.text: Die neue Regierung will das Land im Eilverfahren von "verlängerter Werkbank" auf "wissensbasierte Ökonomie" umpolen.
Seit der Präsidentschaft Richard Nixons wollen sie das Verfassungsgericht umpolen, weil sie es für eine Bastion der Linken halten.

Rettet die Moralisierung des Marktes (»Kauft klimafreundlich«) den Kapitalismus vor seinem Untergang und die Menschheit vor der Katastrophe? Wenn ja, dann müsste es gelingen, die eiserne Marktlogik durch Moralisierung vollständig umzupolen, und zwar von Exzess auf Askese – von Wachstum und Verschwendung auf Schonung und Ressourcenerhaltung.

glosses: verwisselen van de polen (elektriciteit: + of -, magnetisme: zuidpool en noordpool)
To become something different.

examples.text: The tadpole changed into a frog.
Stock prices are constantly changing.

glosses: To make something into something else.

examples.text:
Lo I the man, whoſe Muſe whilome did maske,
As time her taught in lowly Shepheards weeds,
Am now enforſt a far unfitter taske,
For trumpets ſterne to chaunge mine oaten reeds,
And ſinge of Knights and Ladies gentle deeds[…]

KORRIS: They shunned you. Cursed you. Called you vile names, and you knew not why. Even now do you know why you are driven? Why you cannot relent—or repent—or confess—or abstain? How could you know? There have been no other Klingons to lead you to that knowledge.
WORF: Yes—yes—those feelings are still a part of me, but I control them. They do not rule me.
KORRIS: Yes, to fit in, the humans demand you change the one thing that you cannot change. But because you cannot—you do. That too is the mark of the warrior.

glosses: To replace.

examples.text: Ask the janitor to come and change the lightbulb.
After a brisk walk, I washed up and changed my shirt.
Towards the end of the nineteenth century, boys who had pretended soldiers down through the centuries, now changed their pikes and swords for toy pistols.

glosses: To replace one's clothing.

examples.text: You can't go into the dressing room while she’s changing.
The clowns changed into their costumes before the circus started.

glosses: To replace the clothing of (the one wearing it), especially to put a clean diaper on (someone).

examples.text: It’s your turn to change the baby.

glosses: To transfer to another vehicle (train, bus, etc.)

examples.text: After stopping at these stations, my train has become busy. Returning day-trippers make up a goodly number, along with young people heading for a night out in Bristol, which is where I change once again.

glosses: To exchange.

examples.text: At the first sight / they have changed eyes. (exchanged looks)
I would give any thing to change a word or two with this person.

glosses: To change hand while riding (a horse).

examples.text: to change a horse

glosses: The process of becoming different.

examples.text: The product is undergoing a change in order to improve it.

glosses: Small denominations of money given in exchange for a larger denomination.

examples.text: Can I get change for this $100 bill, please?

glosses: A replacement.

examples.text: a change of clothes

After beating champions Chelsea 3-1 on Boxing Day, Arsenal boss Arsene Wenger made eight changes to his starting XI in an effort to freshen things up, with games against Birmingham and Manchester City to come in the next seven days.

glosses: Balance of money returned from the sum paid after deducting the price of a purchase.

examples.text: A customer who pays with a 10-pound note for a £9 item receives one pound in change.

glosses: An amount of cash, usually in the form of coins, but sometimes inclusive of paper money.

examples.text: Do you have any change on you? I need to make a phone call.
This bus ride requires exact change.

glosses: A transfer between vehicles.

examples.text: The train journey from Bristol to Nottingham includes a change at Birmingham.
It [the Elizabeth Line] will provide a 6tph (trains per hour) service and with a single change at Hayes & Harlington offer services towards Reading.

glosses: A change-up pitch.
Any order in which a number of bells are struck, other than that of the diatonic scale.

examples.text: Four bells admit twenty-four changes in ringing.

glosses: A public house; an alehouse.

examples.text:
1727-1728, Edward Burt, Letters from a Gentleman in the North of Scotland to his Friend in London
They call an alehouse a change.

glosses: To revolve or rotate around a centre.

examples.text: The body was turning round slowly as it fell.

glosses: To turn so as to be facing in the opposite direction.

examples.text: It seemed that there was someone behind me; but when I turned round, no one was there.

glosses: To change one's opinion or attitude (especially when becoming hostile etc.).

examples.text: You can't turn round and blame me all of a sudden.

glosses: To make revolve, rotate.
To put into an opposing position; to reverse.

examples.text: He turned the glass round and examined the other side.

glosses: To make (a ship, airplane etc.) ready for departure.

examples.text: The stopover is very short, and crews will have about 15 minutes to turn the plane round.

The interest of individual ships and merchants frequently clash with the general interest, but at times of pressure there is seldom disagreement on the point that the best arrangements are those which permit the greatest number of vessels to be turned round in any given time.

glosses: To process; to complete work on (something), especially with a view to sending it on in a finished state.

examples.text: New figures are in. We need to turn these round ASAP: the boss wants a report tonight.

glosses: Opposite, contrary; going in the opposite direction.

examples.text: We ate the meal in reverse order, starting with dessert and ending with the starter.

glosses: Pertaining to engines, vehicle movement etc. moving in a direction opposite to the usual direction.

examples.text: He selected reverse gear.

glosses: The opposite of something.

examples.text: Division is the reverse of multiplication.

glosses: The act of going backwards; a reversal.

examples.text: By a reverse of fortune, Stephen becomes rich.

glosses: A piece of misfortune; a setback.

examples.text:

examples.text: I shifted into reverse and was just about to back up when our silly cat walked behind the car! Honk honk, kitty! Get out of there!

examples.text: A pyramid reversed may stand upon his point if balanced by admirable skill.

glosses: To transpose the positions of two things.

examples.text: All trends reverse eventually.

glosses: To return, come back.

examples.text: Bene they all dead, and laide in dolefull herse? / Or doen they onely sleepe, and shall againe reuerse?

glosses: To turn away; to cause to depart.

examples.text: And that old dame said many an idle verse, / Out of her daughter's heart fond fancies to reverse.

glosses: To cause to return; to recall.

examples.text: And to his fresh remembrance did reverse / The ugly view of his deformd crimes.
